\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كلية} (kulliyya)}{كلية (kulliyya)}]{\ar{كلية} (kulliyya) — a faculty}

\label{lesson:AR-C390-kulliyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to force, then the Arabic for stability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كلية}}
\textbf{\ar{كلية}} — \emph{kulliyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a faculty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{درس} \ar{أبي} \ar{في} \ar{كلية} \ar{الطب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{darasa abī fī kulliyyat aṭ-ṭibb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father studied at the faculty of medicine.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كلية}} (\emph{kulliyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be all, the whole\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Kulliyya} is a modern abstract noun from \emph{kull}, all; its use for a college of a university is usually explained as a whole branch of learning.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kulliyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kulliyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darasa abī fī kulliyyat aṭ-ṭibb.} — My father studied at the faculty of medicine.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to force, then the Arabic for stability, then say \emph{kulliyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{كلية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A faculty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تخصص} (takhaṣṣuṣ)}{تخصص (takhaṣṣuṣ)}]{\ar{تخصص} (takhaṣṣuṣ) — a specialization}

\label{lesson:AR-C390-takhassus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for stability, then the Arabic for a faculty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تخصص}}
\textbf{\ar{تخصص}} — \emph{takhaṣṣuṣ} — \textquotedblleft{}a specialization\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تخصص} \ar{أختي} \ar{هو} \ar{الكيمياء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takhaṣṣuṣ ukhtī huwa al-kīmiyāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister's specialization is chemistry.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تخصص}} (\emph{takhaṣṣuṣ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṣ-ṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to single out\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Takhaṣṣuṣ} is the Form V verbal noun, singling oneself out for one thing: a specialization.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takhaṣṣuṣ ukhtī huwa al-kīmiyāʾ.} — My sister's specialization is chemistry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for stability, then the Arabic for a faculty, then say \emph{takhaṣṣuṣ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عميد} (ʿamīd)}{عميد (ʿamīd)}]{\ar{عميد} (ʿamīd) — a dean}

\label{lesson:AR-C390-amid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a faculty, then the Arabic for a specialization.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عميد}}
\textbf{\ar{عميد}} — \emph{ʿamīd} — \textquotedblleft{}a dean\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكلم} \ar{العميد} \ar{مع} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{الجدد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takallama al-ʿamīd maʿa aṭ-ṭullāb al-judud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The dean spoke with the new students.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عميد}} (\emph{ʿamīd}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-m-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to prop up, to support\textquotedblright{} (Lane). An \emph{ʿamīd} is a support, the one others lean on: a chief, and now a dean.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منحة} (minḥa)}{منحة (minḥa)}]{\ar{منحة} (minḥa) — a scholarship}

\label{lesson:AR-C390-minha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a specialization, then the Arabic for a dean.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{منحة}}
\textbf{\ar{منحة}} — \emph{minḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}a scholarship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حصلت} \ar{أختي} \ar{على} \ar{منحة} \ar{من} \ar{الجامعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaṣalat ukhtī ʿalā minḥa min al-jāmiʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister got a scholarship from the university.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{منحة}} (\emph{minḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-n-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to give, to bestow\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{minḥa} is a gift: a grant, a scholarship.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{التحق} (iltaḥaqa)}{التحق (iltaḥaqa)}]{\ar{التحق} (iltaḥaqa) — to enrol}

\label{lesson:AR-C390-iltahaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a dean, then the Arabic for a scholarship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{التحق}}
\textbf{\ar{التحق}} — \emph{iltaḥaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to enrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{التحق} \ar{ابني} \ar{بالجامعة} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iltaḥaqa ibnī bi-l-jāmiʿa hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My son enrolled at the university this year.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يلتحق}, \emph{yaltaḥiq}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{التحق} \ar{بـ} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{التحق}} (\emph{iltaḥaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-ḥ-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to overtake, to catch up\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to attach oneself to: to join, to enrol.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iltaḥaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iltaḥaqa ibnī bi-l-jāmiʿa hādhihi as-sana.} — My son enrolled at the university this year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a dean, then the Arabic for a scholarship, then say \emph{iltaḥaqa} again
\end{itemize}
